images.title: Which coffee is strongest?
images.purpose: Shows three 50 mL coffees as decoction and milk layers so the ratios 1 : 4, 3 : 7 and 2 : 3 can be compared by eye.
images.composition: Three identical tall glasses in a row, evenly spaced, each split into 10 equal horizontal bands. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Each glass is a plain outlined tumbler split into 10 equal bands of 5 mL; the bottom bands are amber (#E69F00) decoction, the top bands are white milk with thin dark outline colour (#2B2B2B) dividers. Left glass: 2 amber bands and 8 white bands, label 'light 1 : 4' under it. Middle glass: 3 amber bands and 7 white bands, label 'regular 3 : 7' under it. Right glass: 4 amber bands and 6 white bands, label 'strong 2 : 3' under it, outlined in reddish purple (#CC79A7). To the left of the first glass, a small pointer to the amber part labelled 'decoction' and a small pointer to the white part labelled 'milk'. Exactly 3 glasses, 30 bands in all, 9 amber bands.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: More decoction for the same milk makes stronger coffee, and the ratio tells you which.
images.description: Shows three 50 mL coffees as decoction and milk layers so the ratios 1 : 4, 3 : 7 and 2 : 3 can be compared by eye.
images.context: Light 10 : 40 = 1 : 4, regular 15 : 35 = 3 : 7, strong 20 : 30 = 2 : 3; each 50 mL, 5 mL per band.
images.teaching_notes: Glasses ordered light to strong left to right; no steam, cups or cafe scenery.

image_decisions.why: Strength is a ratio, and seeing equal glasses with different decoction shares makes the comparison concrete.
